page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-8 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the t2a server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. The architecture allocates exactly one physical core per vCPU with no multi-threading. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across multi-core and memory operations, contrasted by weaker single-core capabilities. The single-core Geekbench score of 1073.0 and Passmark CPU score of 6205.54 fall into the weak category. However, multi-threaded execution scales effectively, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 6000.0 and stress-ng multi-core reaching 14472.4, both registering in the average tier. Memory bandwidth is robust for cached small blocks at 563.91 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read and write speeds drop to 87.42 GB/sec and 47.24 GB/sec respectively. The instance demonstrates average performance in software compilation with a Geekbench clang score of 9005.0 and static web serving throughput of 10.09 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the t2a-standard-8 is its weak single-threaded performance and poor LLM inference capabilities, with text generation on a small 135M model yielding only 32.29 tokens/sec. Additionally, the ARM64 architecture lacks x86-specific instruction sets like AVX or AMX, though it supports AES cryptography. Qualitatively, the dedicated physical cores and balanced memory allocation offer a cost-efficient profile for scale-out workloads that benefit from predictable multi-core execution. This server is suited for general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded web serving, software compilation, and database operations.
